## 1. Purpose

This procedure describes the assembly, operation, and maintenance of
vacuum filtration systems used in the EA Program laboratory. Vacuum
filtration separates suspended solids from liquids by drawing the
liquid through a filter membrane or glass fiber filter under reduced
pressure. It is used across many analytical methods, including soil
and water extract filtration (SOPs L403, L409, L418), microplastics
analysis ([SOP-L308](SOP-L308-microplastics-water.qmd)), chlorophyll
extraction ([SOP-L310](SOP-L310-chlorophyll-extraction.qmd)), and
eDNA concentration ([SOP-L700](SOP-L700-dna-extraction.qmd)).


## 2. Scope

- **Applies to:** All vacuum filtration in EA Program laboratories
  using filter flasks, filter funnels (Buchner, glass frit,
  analytical, or Nalgene disposable units), and Fisher Scientific
  Maxidry vacuum pumps or building vacuum lines
- **Does not apply to:** Syringe filtration (push-through, no vacuum);
  centrifugal ultrafiltration; field filtration of eDNA samples
  (covered in [SOP-F700](../field_sops/SOP-F700-edna-field-sampling.qmd))
- **Location:** SGM 133 and SGM 134


## 3. Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve SOP                                 |
| Lab Manager       | Maintain pumps, replace tubing              |
| Trained Personnel | Operate filtration systems per this SOP     |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use    |


## 4. Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Glassware under vacuum:** Filter flasks (Erlenmeyer with
  sidearm) are under reduced pressure during operation. Cracked or
  starred flasks can implode. Inspect all glassware before each use;
  reject any with visible damage.
- **Chemical:** Filtrates may contain hazardous chemicals (acids,
  solvents). Handle filtrate according to the analytical SOP.
- **Biological:** Samples may contain pathogens. Wear gloves.
- **Sharp edges:** Broken glass fiber filters and fritted glass
  funnels can cut skin. Handle with forceps.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses (mandatory; protects against glass implosion)
- [ ] Nitrile gloves
- [ ] Lab coat

### Emergency Procedures

If a filter flask implodes, do not touch the broken glass. Sweep up
fragments with a brush and dustpan (not hands) and dispose in a
sharps container or labeled "Broken Glass" box. If contaminated with
hazardous chemicals, follow
[SOP-L004 Chemical Spill Response](SOP-L004-chemical-spill-response.qmd).


## 5. Equipment and Materials

### Filtration Hardware

| Item                                  | Qty | Location  | Notes                          |
|:--------------------------------------|:----|:----------|:-------------------------------|
| Fisher Scientific Maxidry vacuum pump | 4   | SGM 134   | Oil-free diaphragm pump        |
| Filter flask (sidearm Erlenmeyer, 500 mL or 1 L) | Multiple | SGM 134 | Borosilicate glass; inspect for cracks |
| Rubber stopper with hole (matched to funnel stem) | Multiple | SGM 134 | Connects funnel to flask      |
| Vacuum tubing (thick-wall rubber or silicone) | -- | SGM 134 | Check for cracks and kinks    |
| In-line vacuum trap (flask or bottle between the filter flask and pump) | 1 per pump | SGM 134 | Prevents liquid from reaching the pump |

### Funnel Types

| Funnel Type                           | Application                              |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Buchner funnel (porcelain or polypropylene) | General filtration with flat filter paper or GF filters |
| Glass frit funnel (sintered glass, various porosities) | Fine filtration; reusable; requires careful cleaning |
| Nalgene analytical filter unit (disposable, sterile, 0.45 um PES) | Sterile filtration for microbiological and eDNA work |
| Millipore glass filter holder (47 mm) | Membrane filtration for water quality (TSS, chlorophyll, microplastics) |

### Filter Media

| Filter Type                           | Pore Size | Application                          |
|:--------------------------------------|:----------|:-------------------------------------|
| Whatman GF/A (glass fiber)            | 1.6 um    | General particulate filtration       |
| Whatman GF/F (glass fiber)            | 0.7 um    | Chlorophyll, DOC                     |
| Whatman 934-AH (glass fiber)          | 1.5 um    | TSS, microplastics (SOP-L308)        |
| Cellulose nitrate membrane            | 0.45 um   | Bacterial enumeration, general       |
| PES membrane (polyethersulfone)       | 0.45 um   | Sterile filtration, eDNA             |
| PVDF membrane                         | 0.45 um   | DOC filtration (low carbon blank)    |
| PTFE membrane                         | 0.45 um   | Organic solvent filtration           |

::: {.callout-note}
Select the filter type and pore size specified in the relevant
analytical SOP. Using the wrong filter can bias results (e.g.,
cellulose acetate filters leach DOC and are unsuitable for carbon
analysis).
:::


## 6. Procedure

### 6.1 Assembly

1. Inspect the filter flask for cracks or stars. Do not use damaged
   flasks.
2. Connect vacuum tubing from the flask sidearm to the vacuum trap
   inlet, and from the vacuum trap outlet to the pump
3. Place the rubber stopper into the neck of the flask
4. Seat the appropriate funnel into the stopper
5. If using a 47 mm filter holder: assemble the base, place the
   filter on the fritted support using forceps (avoid touching the
   filter with fingers), and clamp the funnel top in place

### 6.2 Pre-Wetting or Pre-Combustion (If Required)

- For gravimetric analyses (TSS): pre-dry and pre-weigh the filter
  per the analytical SOP
- For DOC filtration: pre-rinse the filter with 50--100 mL of sample
  or DI water and discard the first rinse (removes filter-leached
  carbon)
- For pre-combusted GF/F filters (chlorophyll, DOC): filters should
  have been fired at 450 C for 4 hours per
  [SOP-L111](SOP-L111-muffle-furnace.qmd) and stored in a clean
  container

### 6.3 Filtration

1. Turn on the vacuum pump. Verify suction by briefly covering the
   funnel opening with a gloved hand (you should feel resistance).
2. Pour the sample into the funnel slowly and steadily. For
   particulate-laden samples, add in small aliquots to avoid
   overloading the filter.
3. Allow the liquid to pass through completely
4. Rinse the funnel walls with a small volume of DI water (or the
   matrix specified in the analytical SOP) to transfer any adhering
   particles to the filter
5. Continue vacuum for 10--30 seconds after the last visible liquid
   has passed through to remove residual moisture (do not over-dry
   if the filter will be extracted for chlorophyll or DOC)
6. Turn off the vacuum pump
7. Carefully disconnect the funnel from the stopper

### 6.4 Filter Handling

1. Remove the filter from the funnel using clean forceps
2. Transfer the filter to the appropriate container per the analytical
   SOP:
   - Aluminum tin (for drying/weighing: TSS)
   - Amber vial with extraction solvent (chlorophyll)
   - Extraction tube (eDNA, microplastics)
   - Petri dish (if storing before analysis)
3. Label the container immediately

### 6.5 Filtrate Handling

1. If the filtrate is the analyte of interest (e.g., dissolved
   nutrients, DOC), transfer it from the filter flask to a labeled
   sample vial using a clean graduated cylinder or by pouring
2. Acidify or preserve the filtrate per the analytical SOP
3. If the filtrate is waste, dispose per
   [SOP-L006](SOP-L006-waste-disposal.qmd)

### 6.6 Cleanup

1. Discard used disposable funnels and filters per the analytical SOP
2. Rinse reusable funnels, stoppers, and filter flasks with DI water
   immediately after use
3. For glass frit funnels: back-flush with DI water, then soak in an
   appropriate cleaning solution (acid bath for inorganic work,
   detergent for general use) per
   [SOP-L101](SOP-L101-glassware-cleaning.qmd)
4. Coil vacuum tubing loosely (do not kink) and store


## 7. Vacuum Pump Maintenance

| Task                                  | Frequency              |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------|
| Check vacuum tubing for cracks/kinks  | Before each use        |
| Empty and clean the vacuum trap       | After each use session |
| Verify pump suction (should reach at least 20 in Hg / 500 mmHg) | Monthly |
| Replace vacuum tubing                 | Annually or when degraded |
| Service pump (diaphragm replacement)  | Per manufacturer schedule or when suction declines |

::: {.callout-important}
Always use a vacuum trap (secondary flask or bottle) between the
filter flask and the pump. If liquid reaches the pump, it can damage
the diaphragm and contaminate the pump internals.
:::


## 8. Quality Control

- For analytical methods requiring pre-weighed filters (TSS),
  follow the weighing QC in the analytical SOP
- For DOC filtration, verify filter blanks by filtering DI water and
  analyzing the filtrate; blank DOC should be less than 0.5 mg/L
- Inspect all glassware for cracks before every use


## 9. Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                    | Disposal Method                          |
|:------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Used filters (non-hazardous)  | Standard trash                           |
| Used filters (hazardous matrix) | Chemical waste per SOP-L006            |
| Filtrate (hazardous)          | Appropriate waste stream per SOP-L006    |
| Filtrate (non-hazardous)      | Drain with water if approved by EH&S     |
| Broken glassware              | Sharps container or "Broken Glass" box   |

## 12. Training Record

Before operating vacuum filtration systems independently, personnel
must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Demonstrate proper assembly of the filtration system (flask,
   stopper, funnel, trap, pump, tubing)
3. Demonstrate correct filter handling with forceps
4. Perform one filtration under supervision
5. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager
